title: Timeline
description: Shared contract between the Studio (which writes this file) and the render worker (which validates and renders it). All asset/audio paths in this document are relative to the folder that contains the timeline.json file itself (the "project folder"), never to the process current working directory.

series.description: Name of the series this episode belongs to, e.g. "Sunny Banks", "Skidmarks", "Shorts".

episode.description: Episode identifier/number, or a short slug for one-off shorts and music videos.

fps.description: Frames per second for the whole render. All frame-based timing in the file is expressed in frames at this rate.

canvas.description: Fixed output canvas size. Every layer's x/y transform is in this canvas's pixel space, independent of any source asset's native resolution. Defaults to 1920x1080 if omitted.

duration.description: How long a scene lasts. Exactly one of `frames` (hand-set), `from_audio` (derived from a single audio file's duration), or `from_dialogue` (derived from every layer's dialogue clips, for scenes built from a script with several lines per character) must be given.

from_audio.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to an audio file. The scene's frame count is round(duration_seconds * fps) + padding_frames.

padding_frames.description: Extra frames appended after the audio ends (e.g. for a held last frame).

from_dialogue.description: The scene's frame count is the latest (layer.timing.start_frame + clip.start_frame + that clip's own audio duration) across every dialogue clip on every layer in the scene (plus padding_frames), i.e. it ends when the last line finishes. At least one layer in the scene must have a non-empty `dialogue` (or legacy single `audio`).

padding_frames.description: Extra frames appended after the last line ends.

audio.description: Optional scene-wide audio bed (music/ambience), mixed into the final render starting at this scene's first frame.

frame_step.description: 1 = recompute every frame (normal). N > 1 = classic cut-out "on Ns" animation: the scene is only re-composited every N frames (including camera and slot/cue state), and the frames in between hold/re-emit the exact same rendered canvas instead of recomputing. This affects the picture's update cadence only -- audio is never stepped and always plays at full, continuous rate regardless of frame_step.

asset.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to the background image. It is fitted to the output canvas; it is NOT assumed to already be canvas-sized.

fit.description: cover: scale to fill the canvas, cropping overflow (no letterboxing). contain: scale to fit entirely inside the canvas, letterboxed with black bars.

anchor.description: Which point of the asset's (post-scale) bounding box is placed at transform.x/transform.y in canvas space. Rotation is applied around this same point: after the image is rotated (which expands the canvas) the compositor places the result so this pivot stays fixed at x/y.

ease.description: How to interpolate from this keyframe to the next one that specifies the same property. linear (default) is a constant-speed lerp; inout is a smoothstep ease-in-out. Taken from the departing keyframe of each pair.

frame.description: Layer-local frame (relative to this layer's timing.start_frame) this sample applies at.

x.description: Canvas-space X of the anchor. Omitted: this keyframe does not change X.

y.description: Canvas-space Y of the anchor. Omitted: this keyframe does not change Y.

scale.description: Uniform scale. Omitted: this keyframe does not change scale.

rotation.description: Degrees, clockwise, around the anchor. Omitted: this keyframe does not change rotation.

frame.description: Layer-local frame (relative to the owning layer's timing.start_frame).

rotation.description: Degrees, clockwise, around this child's own pivot.

x.description: Canvas-space X of the anchor point, in pixels.

y.description: Canvas-space Y of the anchor point, in pixels.

rotation.description: Degrees, clockwise, applied around the anchor point after scaling/flipping. The pivot stays fixed: the rotated (expanded) image is placed so the original anchor point still sits at x/y.

timing.description: When a layer is visible, in scene-relative frames. Omit entirely for a layer visible for the whole scene. `end_from_audio` derives the end frame from an audio file's duration instead of a hand-typed `end_frame`.

end_from_audio.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to an audio file. end_frame = start_frame + round(duration_seconds * fps).

mouth_shape.description: Rhubarb Lip Sync mouth shape code. X is the closed/idle shape. This is the fixed drawing-name set a lipsync-driven slot must use as its `images` keys; non-lipsync slots (hands, blinks, etc.) use whatever drawing names make sense for them.

slot.description: A named drawing-swap slot (Toon Boom/Moho style): a single attachment point that shows exactly one named drawing at a time, held until the next change. A mouth driven by Rhubarb cues, a blinking pair of eyes, and a hand that swaps between fist/flat/point poses are all the same mechanism -- only the driver differs. Drawn on top of its owner (the parent layer, or a specific child -- see `layer.slots` / `child.slots`) at the owner's position plus `offset` (scaled/flipped with the owner).

offset.description: Offset in the owner's local (pre-scale) pixel space, from the owner's anchor/pivot point to where this slot's drawing should be centered. Mirrored in x when the owner is flipped, scaled with the owner, and rotated about the owner's pivot by the owner's current rotation so the slot stays attached when the owner swings.

images.description: Map of drawing name -> image path (relative to the project folder). For a `lipsync`-driven slot these names must be Rhubarb mouth shapes (A-H, X); for a `keyframes`-driven slot they can be anything ("fist", "open", "closed", ...). At minimum provide one entry to use as the fallback; a missing drawing at render time falls back to "X" if present, else the first entry in `images`.

keyframes.description: Held-until-changed drawing changes: sorted by `frame`. Each keyframe is either a single `drawing` (held until the next keyframe) or a `cycle` + `fps` that loops those drawings from this frame until the next keyframe. Frames are relative to this slot's owner's own start_frame (not the scene). Before the first keyframe, the first keyframe's drawing/cycle is used. A scene `frame_step` of N>1 already holds the picture on in-between frames, so the cycle is only evaluated on recomputed frames.

visible_when.description: Optional visibility gate: this slot only draws when each named slot's currently active drawing is in the given list. Names are resolved on the same layer (the layer's own slots and every child's slots). Example: hide a mouth unless a body slot is showing "front".

source.description: "dialogue": instead of a single cues/audio pair, this slot is driven by the owning layer's `dialogue` array (see `layer.dialogue`): each clip's own cues apply within that clip's [start_frame, start_frame + its audio duration) window, and the slot shows the idle shape ("X") in the gaps between lines. This is how a mouth slot handles "many lines per character" -- a single-line lipsync (`cues`/`audio` below) is still available for simpler, non-dialogue-list cases.

cues.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to a Rhubarb JSON cues file. A committed cues file is the primary source of truth: if it already exists on disk at render time it is used directly and Rhubarb is never invoked, which keeps renders deterministic and working with zero Rhubarb install. If omitted while `audio` is given, it defaults to "<audio>.rhubarb.json" and doubles as the cache Rhubarb writes to the first time it runs.

audio.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to a WAV file to run Rhubarb on, used only when the `cues` file does not already exist. If Rhubarb is not installed in that situation, the render does not fail: it warns and the slot falls back to its idle/closed shape for the affected range.

dialogue_text.description: Optional spoken line text passed to Rhubarb (--dialogFile) to improve recognition accuracy when generating cues from audio.

lipsync.description: Resolution order (per cues/audio pair, whether it's this single pair or one of `layer.dialogue`'s clips): 1) if `cues` (or its default path next to `audio`) exists on disk, load it -- Rhubarb is not run. 2) else if Rhubarb is installed, run it on `audio` and cache the result at that path. 3) else warn and fall back to the idle shape; the render still completes.

slot_keyframe.description: Either a held drawing or a looping cycle. Exactly one of `drawing` or (`cycle` + `fps`).

cycle.description: Drawings to loop, in order, from this keyframe until the next.

fps.description: How many cycle drawings to show per second of timeline time (at the document fps). index = floor((frame - keyframe.frame) / document_fps * cycle.fps) % len(cycle).

slots.description: Map of slot name (e.g. "mouth", "eyes", "right_hand") -> slot definition. Slots on the same owner are drawn in the order given here, after that owner's own image.

child.description: A cut-out rig child part (head, arm, hand, ...), nested under a parent layer. The parent's transform (position, scale, flip_x) applies to every child, so flipping or walking the parent on/off-screen keeps all its parts aligned and clipped together; `offset`/`pivot`/`z` are the child's own placement relative to its parent (the layer root, or another child named in `parent`). One level of child-to-child nesting is allowed via `parent`; deeper chains and cycles are rejected at load time.

id.description: Unique id of this child within its parent layer.

asset.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to this part's image.

z.description: Draw order relative to the parent's own base image and sibling children (ascending; the parent's own base image is implicitly z = 0 among its children, so e.g. an arm behind the torso uses z < 0 and one in front uses z > 0). This stacking is local to the parent -- it does not interleave with other top-level scene layers' z.

offset.description: In the parent's local (pre-scale) pixel space, from the parent's anchor point to this child's pivot point. Mirrored in x when the parent is flipped, so rig parts stay attached correctly when the whole character flips.

pivot.description: Which point of this child's own (post-scale) bounding box sits at `offset` -- also the point rotation is applied around. Same enum as a top-level layer's `transform.anchor`.

flip_x.description: Composed with the parent's flip_x (XOR): false (default) means this child simply mirrors along with the parent; true gives it an independent mirror on top of that.

rotation.description: Degrees, clockwise, around this child's own pivot (the pivot stays fixed after rotate+canvas-expand). Independent of the layer's own `transform.rotation` (a rotating layer's rotation is not composed into its children -- see docs/timeline-schema.md). When this child is the `parent` of another child, that grandchild's offset is rotated by this value and the rotations accumulate.

rotation_keyframes.description: Optional animation of this child's rotation, layer-local frames, same interpolation rules as `layer.transform_keyframes`. The static `rotation` is used when this list is omitted or empty.

parent.description: Id of another child on the same layer that this child hangs off. Offset is in that parent's local space and is rotated about the parent's pivot by the parent's current rotation. The parent must exist, must not itself have a parent (only one level of nesting), and must not create a cycle.

slots.description: Drawing-swap slots attached to this child instead of to the parent root (e.g. a mouth slot on a head child, a pose slot on a hand child). Slot offsets rotate with this child's current rotation so e.g. a hand on a forearm stays at the wrist.

dialogue_clip.description: One spoken line's audio, placed at an explicit frame. A character layer carries a *list* of these (see `layer.dialogue`) so a real scene can give one character many lines without a separate layer per line.

audio.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to this line's audio file.

start_frame.description: Frame this clip starts at, relative to the owning layer's timing.start_frame (layer-local). Absolute mix time is scene_start + layer.start_frame + clip.start_frame. Typically computed by the script parser from the running total of prior lines/pauses in the scene minus that layer segment's start, but may be hand-set.

cues.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to this clip's Rhubarb cues JSON. Defaults to "<audio>.rhubarb.json" if omitted -- see the lipsync resolution order under `slot.lipsync`.

text.description: The spoken line text. Used as Rhubarb's --dialogFile hint when cues must be generated from audio, and for the lines.json manifest / a future ElevenLabs generation step. Purely informational for rendering.

estimated.description: True when this line has no audio file yet (a silent preview). The renderer holds the mouth on the rest shape X and mixes silence for the estimated duration instead of failing the render.

estimated_duration_seconds.description: Word-count estimate used when the audio file is missing. The script parser writes this onto the clip; the compositor also accepts the same field from lines.json if the clip itself does not have it.

id.description: Unique id of this layer within the scene.

character_id.description: Optional logical character this layer belongs to, for continuity across scenes and tooling (e.g. the script.txt parser).

prop_id.description: Optional logical location-prop identity (from backgrounds/<location>/staging.json `props`) when this layer is a still object rather than a character. Drawn in the same z-ordered list as character layers; the background stays behind every layer.

asset.description: Path (relative to the project folder) to the layer's own (root/base) image (PNG with alpha recommended).

z.description: Explicit draw order within the scene. Layers are drawn back-to-front in ascending z order; the background is implicitly z = -infinity.

transform_keyframes.description: Optional per-property animation of this layer's x/y/scale/rotation. Frames are layer-local (relative to timing.start_frame). Each property is interpolated independently between keyframes that specify it, held before the first and after the last. Properties never mentioned keep the static `transform` value. flip_x is not keyframed -- flip by adding a new layer. Omit entirely for a pose that never moves.

dialogue.description: This character's spoken lines in the scene, each with its own audio/timing/cues. Every clip's audio is mixed into the final render at scene_start + layer.start_frame + clip.start_frame; a `slots.mouth` with `lipsync.source: "dialogue"` shows each clip's cues within that clip's window and the idle shape between lines.

audio.description: Deprecated single-clip shorthand, kept for backward compatibility: equivalent to `dialogue: [{ audio, start_frame: 0 }]` (the clip begins when the layer becomes visible). Ignored if `dialogue` is also given. Prefer `dialogue` for anything with more than one line.

slots.description: Drawing-swap slots attached directly to this layer's own root image (e.g. a mouth on a single-image character with no separate head part).

children.description: Cut-out rig parts nested under this layer. Optional -- most layers are a single flat image with no children.

frame.description: Scene-relative frame this keyframe applies at.

x.description: Canvas-space X the camera is centered on. Defaults to canvas center.

y.description: Canvas-space Y the camera is centered on. Defaults to canvas center.

zoom.description: 1.0 = no zoom (full canvas visible). >1 zooms in.

camera.description: Optional, minimal virtual camera applied to the fully-composited frame: pans/zooms between keyframes (linearly interpolated) and/or an additive shake. Deliberately simple so it can grow later.
